items.title: Open v2.77.0: move the changelog history out of the index into standards/CHANGELOG.md; fix the changelog typos, the order and the footer stamp
items.spec:
Owner ruling for this run (OWNER_SCOPE item 1 puts WAS-R-03 in scope; the session lead decides C-02): the changelog moves. Release number is v2.77.0 (minor: the amendment process changes), and this is the ONE standard version the whole run produces; every later WS item appends a bullet to the v2.77.0 entry instead of bumping again.
End state:
- New standards/CHANGELOG.md: a short header ('# Ka0s WoW Addon Standard: changelog', one sentence saying the index carries only the current entry and this file carries every earlier one, newest first), then the 99 entries currently at standards/STANDARDS.md:99-253 (v2.76.1 .. v1.0.0) moved verbatim, with exactly three edits: (a) the v2.19.0 entry sits above v2.18.0 (today it is at :218 between v2.17.1 and v2.17.0; WAS-A-18); (b) the v2.6x entry at old :120 reads 'preview-mode' not 'preview-mode-§' (WAS-R-12 / WAS-A-13); (c) old :168 reads 'automated-tests-§3' not 'automated-tests-§?' (WAS-A-13). The name is CHANGELOG.md: it is not at a repo root, so documentation-§1/§3's addon-root ban does not reach it (say so in one clause in CLAUDE.md).
- standards/STANDARDS.md: title becomes '(v2.77.0, <landing date>)'. '## Changelog' keeps only the new v2.77.0 entry (lead sentence: the 2026-10-07 review-and-audit remediation; first bullet: the changelog moved and why, with the 418,659 -> ~36 KB index measurement) followed by the line 'Full history: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).' CHANGELOG.md is listed under '## Related documents' and NOT under '## Sections' (tools follow Sections; history is not normative). The footer drops its date: '**End of index. The normative rules live in the section files linked above.**' (WAS-R-07: the header is the single authority).
- Version stamps rolled to v2.77.0: README.md:160 Status, standards/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md:11, standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md:1, CLAUDE.md:143 ('As of v2.77.0').
- Process wording rewritten to the new home: CLAUDE.md:82-84 (index carries front matter, reading guide, Sections, Related documents and the CURRENT changelog entry; on the next release the previous entry moves to the top of standards/CHANGELOG.md) and :135; standards/README.md:13 (drop 'at its top'), :32 and :63-64; README.md:82 (section A step 4); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Module Map and Documentation map gain a standards/CHANGELOG.md row.
- documentation.md:259 (Tier 1 data-flow row): 'documentation-§1 item 8' -> 'documentation-§1 item 6' (the live half of WAS-A-13; item 6 is '## How <it> works').
- Cross-repo handoff H-01 (owned by the dev-copilot planner, not this item): dev-copilot commands/wow-harvest-standards.md:152 and agents/wow-standards-audit.md:108 must point at standards/CHANGELOG.md / the current-entry-in-index shape; that dev-copilot item depends on WS-01 and lands in the same merge, so no build ever sees one without the other.
items.steps:
1. Record the before size: wc -c standards/STANDARDS.md (expect 418659).
2. Extract lines 99-253 into standards/CHANGELOG.md under the header; move the v2.19.0 line above v2.18.0; apply the two typo fixes.
3. Replace STANDARDS.md ## Changelog with the v2.77.0 entry + 'Full history' pointer; add the Related-documents bullet; strip the footer date; bump the title.
4. Roll the four other version stamps; rewrite the CLAUDE.md / standards/README.md / README.md / ARCHITECTURE.md process wording; fix documentation.md:259.
5. Prove the move is lossless (verify block), then commit 'WS-01: open v2.77.0; changelog history moves to standards/CHANGELOG.md'.
items.verify:
cd ../WowAddonStandards
wc -c standards/STANDARDS.md   # < 60000
grep -c '^- \*\*v' standards/CHANGELOG.md   # 99
grep -c '^- \*\*v' standards/STANDARDS.md   # 1 (v2.77.0)
git show HEAD~1:standards/STANDARDS.md | sed -n '99,253p' | grep '^- \*\*v' | sed 's/preview-mode-§/preview-mode/;s/automated-tests-§?/automated-tests-§3/' | sort > /tmp/a; grep '^- \*\*v' standards/CHANGELOG.md | sort > /tmp/b; diff /tmp/a /tmp/b   # empty
grep -n '^- \*\*v2\.1[789]' standards/CHANGELOG.md   # order v2.19.0, v2.18.0, v2.17.1, v2.17.0
grep -n 'preview-mode-§\|automated-tests-§?\|Authoritative as of' standards/   -r   # nothing
git grep -n 'v2\.76\.1' -- CLAUDE.md README.md standards/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md   # nothing
grep -n 'documentation-§1 item 8' standards/standards/documentation.md   # nothing
tr -dc '\r' < standards/CHANGELOG.md | wc -c   # 0

items.title: This repo keeps its own docs/audits/ and docs/reviews/ stores: rewrite the self-description, register both stores, drop the file count and single-source the roster
items.spec:
The 2026-10-07 audit and review bundles are already committed (RA-00, 63ccc5c). documentation-§8 applies audit-review-history unchanged to a documentation-and-tooling repo, so this repo's prose must stop forbidding them.
- Rewrite CLAUDE.md:11-15 ('This repo does not run audits'), :61-62 ('Audit and review runs are not in this repo') and :107-110 ('Audits are per-repo and frozen ... never here'); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:23-24; README.md:17-18 and :154-155. New sense everywhere: an addon audits itself in its own repo; this repo, being audited too (ADDONS.md documentation-and-tooling table, documentation-§8), keeps its OWN documentation-lane docs/audits/<YYYY-MM-DD>/ and docs/reviews/<YYYY-MM-DD>/ frozen stores (audit-review-history), never edited after the fact. AUDIT.md:3-6, standards/README.md:5-6 and ADDONS.md:5-7/:80-81 are accurate (they are about addon audits) and stay as they are apart from an optional one-clause qualifier.
- CLAUDE.md Layout tree gains 'docs/audits/' and 'docs/reviews/' lines.
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md '## Documentation map' (:69): one directory row each for docs/audits/<date>/ and docs/reviews/<date>/ as frozen stores, modelled on the harvests/<date>/ row (documentation-§3 names frozen stores once as directories).
- DEPENDENCIES.md:14: drop '67 tracked files: 63 Markdown'; restate by kind: 'Markdown only, plus LICENSE, .gitattributes and two logo images' (and, once WS-10 lands, that item adds the script).
- WAS-A-17: README.md:47-49 drops the eleven names and the count and links standards/ADDONS.md; line-endings.md:72-74 replaces the enumeration with 'every addon in ADDONS.md, plus LibKa0s' (CLAUDE.md:78 convention).
- WAS-R-11: standards/ADDONS.md Folder column becomes plain code text (`../../AbsorbTracker/`, no link wrapper) on all 11 addon rows plus the LibKa0s and dev-copilot rows; :16's 'local sibling paths' note stays.
- Changelog: one bullet appended to the v2.77.0 entry.
items.steps:
1. grep the cited passages; rewrite each in place.
2. Add the two map rows and the Layout lines; restate DEPENDENCIES.md:14.
3. Replace the two roster enumerations with ADDONS.md pointers; unwrap the Folder links.
4. Append the changelog bullet; commit 'WS-02: ...'.

items.title: toc-file-§5: the load-bearing denominator covers every position in the listing; AUDIT.md step 4 checks the whole TOC; the worked example is cited by heading
items.spec:
Root cause of cluster C05 (AT-A-04/05, CM-A-03, LH-A-01/15..18 are addon items that cite this one).
- standards/standards/toc-file.md denominator paragraph (~:154-157, 'The denominator this MUST is measured against'): load-bearing positions are established by reading EVERY listed file that binds, reads or writes an NS member (or a library major) at file scope — in modules\ and settings\ as much as *Setup.lua and core\Constants.lua — not only the seam files. Keep the 'not by counting lines' point and the 2026-09-07 history paragraph.
- Add one sentence: a load-bearing constraint may be 'below at least one of X/Y/Z' (LH-A-15 shape); the comment names what resolves, not a single file, when several satisfy it.
- AUDIT.md step 4 'Check the TOC's position annotations (toc-file-§5)' (~:402): 'In the # Core block, every line' -> 'At every position in the listing (# Core, # Defaults, # Modules, # Settings and any other group), every line'; 'Read the seam files (*Setup.lua) and core/Constants.lua' -> 'Read every listed file for file-scope reads/writes of NS members and library majors'.
- toc-file.md:171 worked example (AT-A-14): replace 'AbsorbTracker.toc:35-42' with the block's heading, '# Core (the LibKa0s-Env seam loads first)' in AbsorbTracker.toc (the block actually spans :37-44 today, which is why a line range is the wrong form).
- Changelog bullet appended to v2.77.0 (a clarification of an existing MUST's denominator, no new obligation).
items.steps:
1. Edit toc-file.md denominator paragraph and worked-example citation.
2. Edit AUDIT.md step 4 to match.
3. Append changelog bullet; commit.

items.title: documentation-§3/§6/§8 and library-stack-§7 agree with themselves: §6 cites §3's frozen-store list, §8's arithmetic and single executable-content trigger, the documentation-§5/§6 row labels, ordinals and Tier 2 membership
items.spec:
All in standards/standards/documentation.md unless noted.
- WAS-A-14 (§6 'Frozen bundles are exempt', ~:625-636): delete the private four-store list; cite documentation-§3's frozen/generated list by reference (docs/audits/, docs/reviews/, docs/automated-tests/<run>/, docs/perf-analysis/<run>/, docs/revendor/<date>-v<tag>/, docs/superpowers/, docs/investigations/). Narrow the automated-tests exemption to docs/automated-tests/<run>/ (README.md and RESULTS.md are live). Add a clause for a repo's own frozen stores (this repo's harvests/ and standards/_raw/; a library's equivalents). Replace the grep --exclude-dir sweep with a git ls-files pipeline that excludes every frozen store, e.g. git ls-files -z -- '*.md' ':!:docs/audits/**' ':!:docs/reviews/**' ':!:docs/automated-tests/*/**' ':!:docs/perf-analysis/*/**' ':!:docs/revendor/*/**' ':!:docs/superpowers/**' ':!:docs/investigations/**' ':!:libs/**' ':!:tests/_kit/**' ':!:harvests/**' ':!:standards/_raw/**' | xargs -0 grep -nE '§[0-9]+\.[0-9]' (keeping the 'command, not enumeration' reporting rule).
- WAS-A-12: drop the ordinals at :170 ('the ninth mandated section') and :347 ('the tenth ARCHITECTURE.md section'); refer to the sections by name.
- WAS-A-15 + DC-A-15 (§8): fix the arithmetic at ~:698 so Module Map is counted once (five sections dropped, five kept, one of the five — Module Map — reinterpreted); reword the exhaustiveness claim as file-granular and state that any subsection not listed applies unchanged; place localization-§1-§4 under 'Does not apply' explicitly. The executable-content row (~:703) states ONE trigger: lint/testing/automated-tests are re-read when the repo tracks its first .lua file; any other executable content (a shell or Python script, a non-Lua test harness) MUST instead record in DEPENDENCIES.md how it is verified. Remove the three-trigger sentence. (Ruling: lint/testing/automated-tests presuppose Lua; this keeps dev-copilot's Python helpers and this repo's WS-10 shell script out of the Lua suites while still requiring a recorded verification.)
- LK-A-10 + WAS-R-06 (library-stack.md:223): split the mislabeled row into 'documentation-§5 | Keeping docs in sync.' and 'documentation-§6 | The filename-§N citation scheme and its citation rules.' so the §4 row's 'already named' cross-reference (~:261) holds; add the same 'any subsection not listed applies unchanged; the lists are file-granular' sentence to library-stack-§7's exhaustiveness paragraph (~:205). AUDIT.md:994 'documentation-§5/§6' -> 'documentation-§6'.
- WAS-A-16: in CLAUDE.md (~:155-156) and standards/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md:38, the Tier 2 parenthetical notes that perf-analysis/README.md is also a Tier 2 member, its trigger stated under verification-and-record.
- Changelog bullet appended to v2.77.0.

2. Ordinals; §8 arithmetic, exhaustiveness wording, localization placement, single trigger.

items.title: documentation-§6 gains a cross-repo citation SHOULD (symbol/heading for present tense, Repo@sha:path:line for history); convert the rotted citations and misleading counts to it
items.spec:
- New SHOULD in documentation-§6 (after the citation-scheme rules): a claim about another repo's code cites, in present tense, `Repo path` plus a symbol or heading (never a bare line number); a historical claim pins the commit, `Repo@<sha>:path:line`. A present-tense count or inventory is written as a rule ('every addon ...') or dated ('as measured on 2026-10-07'). Rationale: 43 of 61 cross-repo citations had moved and 6 named missing files (docs/audits/2026-10-07/03_EVIDENCE.md E5).
- Convert every citation in that E5 table that no longer matches (the 43 moved + 6 gone) — e.g. options-ui.md:410, standalone-windows.md:31/:34/:37, documentation.md:392-393/:416-418, library-stack.md:382-388 — to symbol/heading form or SHA-pin it; past-tense or delete the 6 gone claims (MultiMeters/settings/Schema.lua:1553-1566 in a 1392-line file; 'Five addons ship a private core/LSMPatch.lua' — none does).
- WAS-A-10: AUDIT.md:522-523 and standalone-windows.md:34 cite BankLedger 'B:MakeCloseButton' (modules/Browser.lua) by symbol, not :98.
- WAS-A-11 (no full recount): layout.md:93 PrettyChat splitter is tools/split_globalstrings.py — retire it as a known instance; EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY 'all eleven addons wrote' vs 'nine of nine' made consistent; EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md:52 'the eight addons' CRLF -> 'every addon in ADDONS.md'; other present-tense counts at audit-review-history.md:9/:11/:25/:51, AUDIT.md:145-146/:270/:343-348, documentation.md:150/:297-305/:359 ('Ten addons ship the re-vendor store'), library-stack.md:95, open-evolutions.md:71, options-ui.md:376/:408 reworded as rules or dated; history files get date stamps only.
- WAS-R-09: testing.md:292 'revision 24 ships today' -> 'LibKa0s test-kit revision 24 and later ship this'; testing.md:20 and NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md:1019 describe tests/_kit/ as 'vendored whole from LibKa0s testkit/, never edited' instead of a 4-of-22 file list.
- LK-A-08: library-stack.md:118 (Inter-module dependencies) cites the Options->Pool floor by symbol (the NEEDS_POOL floor) and names all three attach files: OptionsWidgets.lua, OptionsTabs.lua and OptionsNav.lua (no line numbers).
- Changelog bullet appended to v2.77.0.
items.steps:

items.title: versioning-git: default-branch work by default, owner-directed or multi-repo changesets on a same-named feat/<date>-<topic> branch merged --no-ff; ripple to the index blurb, context pack, anti-pattern #21, documentation-§8 and CLAUDE.md
items.spec:
Ruling (cluster C32): the trunk-based MUST is revised to match how the collection actually works; no per-repo deviation rows are filed (DC-A-12 becomes moot).
- standards/standards/versioning-git.md:13 replaced by: work lands on the repo's default branch by default; a changeset the owner directs to be isolated, or one that spans several repos, goes on feat/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<topic>, the SAME name in every repo it touches, merged into the default branch with --no-ff and then deleted (branch, and any worktree or stash the run created). Merging, tagging, pushing and releasing keep their owner go-ahead gates (the existing 'MUST NOT push unless the human asks' stays, with 'push a feature branch at a checkpoint the owner authorized' as the sanctioned case). Use repo-kind-neutral wording ('the repo's default branch', not 'the addon's') because documentation-§8 and library-stack-§7 bind this section to all three kinds.
- Ripple: STANDARDS.md:78 Sections blurb ('semver; default-branch work with owner-directed feature branches; commit only on green'); standards/standards/anti-patterns.md #21 -> 'Creating a feature/topic branch the owner did not direct, or one not shared by name across the repos of a multi-repo changeset' (number unchanged, range stays #1-#92); NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md:1520 git rule 23 and :1576 anti-pattern line; documentation.md:676 §8 versioning-git row; library-stack-§7 versioning-git row (:220) if it says trunk; CLAUDE.md:116-117 Git workflow aligned to the same wording.
- Changelog bullet appended to v2.77.0.
items.steps:
1. Rewrite versioning-git §1 git-workflow bullet.
2. Apply the ripple sites listed; grep -i trunk across live docs.
3. Changelog bullet; commit.

items.spec:

items.title: scripts/check-standard.sh: an on-demand mechanical gate for the standard's own invariants (CR bytes, .gitattributes body, citation ranges, Sections list, anti-pattern contiguity, version stamps, roster pointers)
items.spec:
New scripts/check-standard.sh (bash, LF via the *.sh carve-out, executable, set -u), run on demand and by sync-docs — NOT a commit hook (CLAUDE.md 'two checkpoints'). Each check prints its failures and the script exits non-zero if any fails; exit 0 on the tree:
 1. No CR byte in any tracked file (git grep -Il $'\r').
 2. .gitattributes equals line-endings-§5's LF body (the second column-0 ```gitattributes fence in line-endings.md).
 3. Every filename-§N in live docs names an existing standards/standards/<filename>.md and an existing '### N.' heading; any -§N against one of the eleven unnumbered files fails; a bare '-§' or '-§?' fails. Excluded: harvests/, standards/_raw/, docs/audits/, docs/reviews/, standards/CHANGELOG.md (history: numbers were right when written).
 4. STANDARDS.md ## Sections links == git ls-files 'standards/standards/*.md'.
 5. anti-patterns.md is numbered 1..N contiguously and the index blurb says (#1–#N).
 6. The STANDARDS.md title version appears in README.md Status, EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md, NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md:1 and CLAUDE.md 'As of' line.
 7. Internal relative .md links resolve (excluding ADDONS.md sibling-folder paths and frozen stores).
Docs: DEPENDENCIES.md required list gains bash and coreutils/grep/awk with a Verify column; 'no test runner' becomes 'one on-demand check script'; 'Verifying your setup' runs bash scripts/check-standard.sh; the by-kind file line gains the script. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: Module Map row; Known Limitations 'No mechanical gate' / 'Cross-references are unenforced' rewritten to what is now covered and what is not (semantic contradictions, wrong-but-in-range citations). CLAUDE.md Editing rules: run the script before committing a change to the standard; Layout tree gains scripts/. documentation-§8 (as ruled in WS-05) means a .sh does not pull in lint/testing; DEPENDENCIES.md records how the script is verified. Changelog bullet appended to v2.77.0.
items.steps:
Test-first, without temporary files in the repo:
1. Write the injected-defect harness in the scratchpad: clone the repo (git clone ../WowAddonStandards <scratch>/ws), and for each check script one defect (add a CR to a .md; drop '*.py text eol=lf' from .gitattributes; write 'toc-file-§99' and 'compat-§1' into a live doc; remove a Sections link; renumber an anti-pattern; change README's version). Each must make the script exit non-zero, naming the check.
2. Implement scripts/check-standard.sh until all seven injections go red and the clean tree goes green.
3. Document in DEPENDENCIES.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and CLAUDE.md; changelog bullet; commit; delete the scratch clone.
items.verify:
cd ../WowAddonStandards
bash scripts/check-standard.sh; echo $?   # 0
git check-attr eol -- scripts/check-standard.sh   # lf
test -x scripts/check-standard.sh
scratch clone: each of the seven injected defects -> exit != 0 with the named check
grep -n 'check-standard.sh' DEPENDENCIES.md docs/ARCHITECTURE.md CLAUDE.md   # all three
